summary: Frontend e2e test of the new now-playing visualizer placed behind the album art. STRUCTURAL checks all pass (canvas exists, correct z-index layering, exactly one canvas, no console errors, playback advances). However a CRITICAL rendering bug was confirmed: the visualizer canvas never actually draws anything — it is 100% blank. The 'glow' visible behind the album art in the screenshot is only the album-art's own boxShadow, not the visualizer waves the user requested.

ui_bugs.issue: Visualizer canvas renders BLANK. Internal canvas dimensions remain the HTML defaults (width=300, height=150) — the `canvas.width = 520; canvas.height = 300;` lines never execute. getImageData on the canvas returns 0 non-zero-alpha pixels out of 45000. Root cause: the useEffect has `[]` deps so it runs once on mount, but on first render `loading=true` causes the component to early-return a spinner (lines 304-306), so canvasRef.current is null. The effect hits `if (!canvas) return;` and exits. When loading later flips false and the <canvas> mounts, the []-dep effect never re-runs, so no animation loop is started and `canvas.width/height` are never set. Result: no waves are drawn behind the album art; only the album's own boxShadow glow is visible.

issues: Because the visualizer never draws, the now-playing screen does NOT visually match the landing page's animated waves around the YOURFM logo. The user-reported regression is therefore NOT fixed.

action_items: Fix Player.jsx visualizer useEffect so it runs AFTER the canvas mounts. Simplest fix: change the deps from `[]` to `[loading]` (and keep the `if (!canvas) return;` guard) so the effect re-runs once loading flips false and canvasRef.current is non-null. Alternative: move the early `if (loading) return <spinner/>` AFTER the JSX so the canvas mounts unconditionally; or render the canvas regardless of loading and only conditionally render the album art/controls.

After the fix, re-verify: (a) canvas.width === 520 and canvas.height === 300 at runtime, (b) getImageData reports >0 non-zero-alpha pixels (waves drawn), (c) screenshot shows purple+gold glowing waves around the album art matching the landing page aesthetic.
critical_code_review_comments: Player.jsx is 414 lines — within limits, fine.
Visualizer useEffect deps `[]` is the root of the bug; it must depend on whether the canvas is mounted (i.e., on `loading` or use a callback ref).
Consider using a callback ref pattern (ref={node => { if (node) startViz(node); }}) instead of useRef+useEffect — eliminates this entire class of mount-timing bugs.
Web Audio graph correctly connects to <audio> and resumes context on play; no issues there.
All required data-testids are present and correctly wired.
seed_data_creation: Created 1 test station 'TEST_VizStation' via the UI (in addition to the 2 already present from prior iterations).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Test stations exist in DB already, you can skip creation and go straight to clicking an existing station card. The structural checks (canvas exists, z-index 1 vs 10, overlap with album-art, single canvas, no console errors, playback advances) all PASS. The only failing check is the FUNCTIONAL one: canvas pixels are blank because the useEffect ran while the component was still rendering the loading spinner. After main agent's fix, run the same `getImageData` check to confirm non-zero pixels are drawn.

rca_of_the_issue.bug: Visualizer canvas behind album art renders nothing (0 pixels drawn).
rca_of_the_issue.reproduction: 1) Open app, click start-listening-btn. 2) Click an existing station card (or create one). 3) Wait for player-container. 4) Run document.querySelector('[data-testid=visualizer-canvas']).getContext('2d').getImageData(0,0,300,150).data — every alpha byte is 0. Also check canvas.width===300 (default), not 520.
rca_of_the_issue.root_cause: Player.jsx line 72-120 useEffect has [] deps. On initial mount, `loading` is true and the component returns the spinner (line 304-306) before the canvas JSX renders, so canvasRef.current is null when the effect runs. The effect's `if (!canvas) return;` guard exits silently. When loading later flips to false and the canvas mounts, the []-dep effect does NOT re-run — so canvas.width/height are never set and requestAnimationFrame is never scheduled.
rca_of_the_issue.mitigation: Change the useEffect deps from `[]` to `[loading]` (keeping the !canvas guard). Or remove the early `if (loading) return <spinner/>` and render the canvas + spinner overlay together. Or use a callback ref to start the animation the moment the canvas node is attached.
